node.title: Re: print all files is soo slow! Why?
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Hi [harangzsolt33],

The problem you're experiencing does sound strange to me, especially with the behavior you describe [id://1168528|here], but it's been a while since I worked with Perl on the command line in Windows - the explanations by the AM ([id://1168521|here]) seem plausible if you're trying to print lots of binary data.

I just wanted to point out that Perl has an operator that tries to tell "text" from "binary" files based on a heuristic: [doc://-X|-T] (the heuristic is described in the documentation).

Also, while walking a directory tree yourself is certainly a useful exercise, there are modules to help you, here's one example with [mod://Path::Class]:

use warnings; use strict; use Path::Class qw/file dir/; my $PATH = dir('.'); $PATH->recurse( callback => sub { my $file = shift; return if $file->is_dir || -B $file; my $fh = $file->open('<:raw') or return; read $fh, my $content, 2000 or return; close $fh; print $content; } );

Just a small note, in your current code you have a few variables that could have better scoping. $CONTENT could be defined right before its use in [doc://read], then you don't have to clear it every time. And the $SUB you define at the beginning of explore is actually never used because it is shadowed by the second $SUB in the while loop.

Hope this helps,
-- Hauke D
